scope: Independent adversarial review of R6 source changes from verified R5. Production code was read only; this reviewer authored only this report.
verified_checks: HUD-less format observations converge without the R5 static-format/global-pause feedback loop; failed SDK tags erase poisoned map entries without using erased aliases.

Recovery enables the SDK before new resource tags, requires same-frame accepted depth/motion/constants and expected HUD-less input, and confirms only a matching coherent non-TEST native Present with successful SDK status and more than one queued frame.
Four stamped evidence slots preserve older ready frames when future inputs arrive; ordinary one-frame Streamline counter correction cannot restart recovery.

Expected-active observation tokens detect two unexpected disabled statuses but cannot heal an incomplete frame or fault on its missing-input negative result. Ambiguous/query-warning/native-nonzero samples are excluded.
Retry actions are bounded and serialized. Terminal provider/context errors stop retries, including control-call errors; soft alias resets preserve that stop until provider context recreation.
Existing R5 work/present/submission admission and GPU-resource ownership remain intact; no new Evict, forced game-resource Release, or timeout-driven resource destruction was introduced.

Allocation accounting retains no GPU object references, balances temporary QI references, uses generation-checked bounded callback storage, and explicitly reports partial creation estimates rather than residency.
Allocation installer/uninstaller preserve trampoline state on transaction failure, skip conflicting native method addresses, share legacy base-hook ownership, and support bounded retry.
Residency calls forward once and preserve original failures except the known AMD XeFG/XeSS E_INVALIDARG compatibility case.
FFX context registry operations use short locks around shared map access; provider calls run outside the lock and destroy takes routing metadata atomically.
R6 does not change shader/color/exposure/upscale or multiplier policy. Listed configuration, unlock and pacing source files match verified R5 byte for byte.

independently_executed_checks.coverage: Pinned R5 negative controls; production helper and extracted resource/dispatch/control functions; healthy and trial status; bounded retries; terminal outcomes; SL1 frame boundary; actual callback/COM adapter and hook transaction fault injection.
Production registry helper; 16000 concurrent context lifetimes; exactly one atomic Take winner; fallback routing.

runtime_limitations: No Cyberpunk 2077, Night City-to-Dogtown transition, Intel XeFG GPU execution, visual-quality comparison, or long-session FPS measurement was performed by this reviewer.
CPU harnesses execute production logic with fake SDK/COM/driver boundaries; Windows build, real Detours ABI/runtime behavior and device-specific SDK behavior require separate CI/runtime validation.

R5 logs correlate rising local-memory pressure with slow native Present, but do not identify the allocating owner or prove that the repaired format/tag/registry defects caused the reported Dogtown slowdown.
Provider queued-frame status is not GPU completion or measured display FPS; passing recovery tests does not guarantee performance recovery under true memory or driver pressure.

Allocation provenance is partial: supported APIs and allocations at least 1 MiB observed after hooks, bounded 4096 slots, immediate caller module attribution, and notifier availability. Estimates and provisional peak counters are not resident VRAM.
The callback module and one fixed CPU ledger deliberately live until process exit; game GPU allocations are not pinned by this accounting.
Inherited UI-fence/full-teardown GPU waits can still block; this change does not claim to remove every existing wait or to repair arbitrary device removal.

portability_followups.issue: Windows MSVC C2169 rejected defining a fake function named _ReturnAddress, which is a compiler intrinsic.
portability_followups.change: Harness-only FakeReturnAddress function plus a preprocessor redirect for the extracted production call; assertions and production code unchanged.
